drafts.title: $29,990 Cybercab, then $299 a month or it won't move
drafts.angle: Cheapest Tesla ever, but it's a subscription car. Even Musk says the fee is too high. Who is it really for, and at what monthly price would you buy?
bullets: Tesla invited select customers Nov 13 to order Cybercab for personal use: $29,990 before tax, $1,000 non-refundable deposit, estimated December 2026 delivery in Austin.
A $299 per month Autonomy Subscription is required to operate it (first month included). That's $3,588 a year.
Only works inside Robotaxi service areas (Texas and Florida cities to start). Personal use only, no ride-hail.
Musk said "the monthly fee is too high" and suggested closer to FSD plus connectivity, about $115 a month (Reuters, per pack).
drafts.body: $29,990 for a Tesla with no steering wheel. Then $299 a month or it won't move. That's $3,588 a year before insurance. Musk himself says the fee is too high. My Model Y costs me {my monthly FSD or charging number}. At what monthly price would you buy one?
drafts.framework_body:
$29,990 for a Tesla with no steering wheel.

Then $299 a month, or it doesn't move. That's $3,588 a year before insurance and charging.

Tesla opened personal Cybercab orders to select customers this week. $1,000 down, delivery in Austin as soon as December. Catch: it only works inside Robotaxi zones, so Texas and Florida cities first. Out here in Colorado it would be a very expensive lawn ornament for now.

Even Musk says the monthly fee is too high and floated something closer to $115.

Here's who I think this is really for once it spreads: folks who can't or shouldn't drive anymore, and families juggling a teen and two jobs. For them, a car that drives itself could mean staying independent longer.

For me today, my Model Y costs {my monthly FSD or charging number}. {my one-line take: would I buy one}

At what monthly price would you buy one?
drafts.ocr_why: Hottest EV debate of the day, dollar opener, clean poll-style price question, independence angle for 55+.
drafts.pixel: Quick talk-to-camera: "Thirty grand plus three hundred a month. Here's who I think it's for."
drafts.premium_target: Quote Sawyer Merritt's Cybercab order post with one line: "$299 a month is the real price tag. Who's it for?"

drafts.title: $20 a month: Xcel credit for Coloradans 65+, and bills dipped 3%
drafts.angle: Rare good news on a power bill, plus money seniors may be leaving on the table. A save-and-share for anyone with parents in Colorado.
bullets: Xcel Colorado Q4 2026 fuel adjustment fell to $0.02520 per kWh; average residential bill (601 kWh) went from $101.96 to $98.89, down 3.01%.
The PUC rate case (Aug 2026) created a $20 per month bill credit for income-qualified seniors 65 and up.
Winter flat rate base is $0.0857 per kWh plus a $7.10 service charge and riders.
Xcel Optimize Your Charge pays EV owners a $50 yearly credit if 80% of charging lands in the 12 AM to 2 PM window.
drafts.body: $20 a month. That's a new Xcel credit for income-qualified Coloradans 65 and up. Average bills also dipped 3% this quarter. My bill with an EV in the garage: {my monthly number}. Know someone 65+ who should check if they qualify?
drafts.framework_body:
$20 a month.

That's a bill credit most Colorado seniors have never heard of. The PUC created it this year for income-qualified Xcel customers 65 and up. That's $240 a year back.

And a rare bit of good news for everybody else: the average Xcel residential bill dipped about 3% this quarter, from $101.96 to $98.89, because fuel costs came down.

If you drive an EV, there's another one. Xcel pays $50 a year if most of your charging happens overnight or midday.

My own bill with an EV in the garage: {my monthly number} on {my utility}. {photo of my bill with the account number blurred}

This is the kind of thing that never gets mailed to you in plain English. Call Xcel or check your account and ask about the senior credit.

Know someone 65+ in Colorado who should check if they qualify?
drafts.ocr_why: Pocketbook, 55+ audience, tell-your-parents save and share, dollar opener.
drafts.pixel: Hold up the bill with the account number blurred: "Here's my bill with an EV. And here's a credit seniors should ask about."
drafts.premium_target: Reply to a verified Colorado news or energy-bill thread (Denver7, Colorado Sun, CPR) with the $20 senior credit tip.

drafts.title: {$XX a month} in forgotten subscriptions: I asked my phone
drafts.angle: AI for normal people: your phone can now tell you what you're still paying for and what went up. It can read your spending but can't move a dime.
bullets: Google, Nov 13: all US Gemini app users can connect Google Wallet; bank and card accounts link via Plaid.
Ask "what subscriptions am I still paying for, and did any go up this year?" and it flags recurring charges and price hikes.
Read-only: Google says Gemini can't move, manage, or invest your money. Opt-in, turn off anytime.
It can also help set a holiday budget from last year's spending.
drafts.body: {$XX a month} in subscriptions I forgot about. That's what my Pixel found when I asked Gemini. It can read your spending now, but it can't move a dime. What's the one subscription you'd bet you're still paying for?
drafts.framework_body:
{$XX a month}.

That's what I was paying for subscriptions I forgot about. I found it by asking my phone one question.

As of this week, Gemini on any US phone can connect to Google Wallet and your bank accounts. I asked it: what subscriptions am I still paying for, and did any go up this year?

It came back with {what it found, e.g. number of subscriptions and the biggest surprise}.

The part that matters for anyone nervous about AI: it's read-only. It can look, it can't move a dime. You opt in and can shut it off anytime.

This is what AI for regular people should look like. Not a robot taking over. A helper that finds the $12 charge you forgot about in 2023.

If you help a parent with their bills, this could be a 5-minute holiday project.

What's the one subscription you'd bet you're still paying for?
drafts.ocr_why: Strong if he actually tries it (first-hand result). Fits the AI-less-scary push. Distinct from his ChatGPT Wallet post: read-only budgeting, not AI shopping.
drafts.pixel: Screen-record the question on the Pixel: "I asked my phone what I forgot to cancel. Here's what it said."
drafts.premium_target: Quote Google's or a big verified Android/Pixel account's Gemini Wallet launch post with your found number.
